title: The Perfect Prescription: Puerto Rico Delivered Better Results, but Washington Wants a Second Opinion.
description: Puerto Rico built a high-performance, adherence-first pharmacy model that ranks #1 of all 56 U.S. jurisdictions for both the highest prescription utilization and the lowest gross drug costs - filling about 19% more prescriptions a year while paying roughly 30% less per fill ($63 vs. $89 nationally). This episode traces how community pharmacies - through the AFCPR medication-adherence program launched in 2013 under Elliot Pacheco - turned adherence into five-star Medicare Advantage performance, and why a statutory blind spot still boxes the island out of the low-income subsidies the 50 states get automatically: an estimated $250 million in foregone assistance every year, and up to $2 billion under full parity. Better results, less money - so why does Washington want a second opinion?
